---
title: "PSY221A: Correlation, t-test, and ANOVA"
output: html_document
---

## 1. Load the processed data

```{r load}
# Open the project's .Rproj file before running chunks.

h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2.csv")

# Check the variable types, missing values, and group sizes.
str(h1Data)
str(h2Data)
table(h2Data$Sex_birth, useNA = "ifany")

```

## 2. H2: Correlation

```{r correlation}
# cor() gives the correlation coefficient
cor(h1Data$percMoral, h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1)

# cor.test() gives a hypothesis test and a confidence interval for two continuous intervals.
# The default is a two-sided Pearson correlation test.
# The null hypothesis is that the population correlation is zero.
cor.test(h1Data$percMoral, h1Data$Love_would_you_marry_1)

# The 95% confidence interval describes uncertainty about the population correlation.
```

## 3. H1: Independent-samples t-test

```{r t_test for Sex_birth with only Male and Female}
# For t-test, we will compare Male and Female respondents only.
# Keep the original h1Data unchanged.
h2Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h2Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels= c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

h2Ttest <- h2Data[h2Data$Sex_birth %in% c("Male","Female"),]

# Check the groups and their descriptive statistics before testing.
table(h2Ttest$Sex_birth)
by(h2Ttest$Time_A_dress_1, h2Ttest$Sex_birth, mean)

# The null hypothesis is that the two population means are equal.
# Conduct independent sample t-test
t.test(Time_A_dress_1 ~ Sex_birth, data=h2Ttest) # Outcome variable first

# Read the group means to see which group allocated more points on average.
# t is the test statistic, df is the degrees of freedom, and p-value evaluates the null hypothesis.
```

## 4. H1: One-way ANOVA

```{r anova}
# Return to h1Data to compare Male, Female, and Intersex respondents.
by(h2Ttest$Time_A_dress_1, h2Ttest$Sex_birth, mean)

# The null hypothesis is that all three population means are equal.
# Save the ANOVA model, then use summary() to display the ANOVA table.
h2Anova <- aov(Time_A_dress_1 ~ Sex_birth, data=h2Data)

# A significant result indicates that at least one population mean differs.
```

## 5. Which groups differ?

```{r post_hoc}
# After ANOVA, Tukey's test compares each pair of groups while adjusting for multiple comparisons.
tuk <- TukeyHSD(h2Anova)
options(width = 120, digits = 15) # Looked up adjusted options since it was so significant R was cutting it off!
print(tuk)

# diff is the first named group's mean minus the second named group's mean in each comparison label.
# lwr and upr are the confidence limits; p adj is the adjusted p-value.
```
